core_statement: For a cap-one probability density f and any positive subdensity rho of mass m, f*tilde(rho) has mass m and density cap at most m; after normalization it is again cap one. Arbitrary finite/countable product localization of one duplicated copy therefore becomes an exact convex mixture of cap-one product difference laws.

fixed_source.applied_inequality: For M=(1/sqrt(2))*[(e1),(e1),(e2),(e2),(e3),(e3)], M^T M=I, Z=1 and all row marginals=1/2, so ||p_Q||_infinity <= 6 sqrt(e). Original-tooth-first localization costs 6 sqrt(e) N on N equal teeth; decouple-first one-copy localization retains 6 sqrt(e).

partner.result_used: Gaussian-mixture inverse-half-scale moment implies BV control; N-fragment comb approximation requires asymptotic cost N sqrt(2pi).
partner.application: The new exact post-decoupling difference-law localization bypasses this pre-decoupling regularization obstruction without approximating the rough marginal.

countable_stress: For tooth masses m_k proportional to 1/[k(log(k+1))^2] on arbitrarily remote intervals, fragment-first original-variable Theorem-D certificates sum as 6 sqrt(e)(sum m_k^(2/3))^3=+infinity, while whole/decouple-first remains 6 sqrt(e).
next_step: Prove a structural product-preserving partition from bare s3(A)>=1 that exposes a D/D'/D5/projected-crossing receiver while routing rough localization to the difference-side copy, or force another whole-law receiver before oscillatory-side normalization.
